metadata.title: DC Vision Zero High-Injury Corridors
metadata.description: Top 8 HIN corridors by people killed or seriously injured, computed by joining Open Data DC crashes to the DDOT High Injury Network.
metadata.source_title: Crashes in DC x High Injury Network
metadata.method: Each crash since 2022-01-01 is assigned to the nearest HIN corridor whose centerline passes within 25 m (point-to-segment, local equirectangular projection). KSI = people killed + seriously (major) injured. Injuries = all reported injured people (major + minor). Ward(s) are read from the joined crash records. Each corridor carries an `audit` block (date range, join-distance stats, and a sample of CRIMEID record IDs) and `totals` reports fetched/geocoded/joined/excluded counts so the figures are traceable back to source records. Recommended interventions are a screening suggestion ranked by the corridor's own mode mix and severity (each carries its trigger), not a DDOT plan; effect sizes come from data/countermeasures.json (research-grade until verified).
metadata.caveats: Counts are crashes within 25 m of the DDOT High Injury Network centerline, 2022-present, from the open, police-reported Crashes in DC dataset; they may differ from DDOT's curated figures. Ungeocoded crashes and crashes off the HIN are excluded. A crash near two corridors is assigned to the nearest.

properties.location_scope: 7th St NW/Florida Ave NW To Chesapeake St NW

recommended_interventions.name: Automated speed enforcement
recommended_interventions.effect: A DDOT study reported injury crashes falling from 841 to 673 (about -20% injuries) around enforced locations; Portland measured -71% to -93% top-end speeding within 30 days of activation.

recommended_interventions.name: Road diet / lane rechannelization
recommended_interventions.effect: FHWA cites ~19-47% total crash reductions for road diets; Seattle's Nickerson St saw roughly -93% aggressive (top-end) speeding.

recommended_interventions.name: Protected intersections
recommended_interventions.effect: Widely deployed in Vision Zero programs to remove turning conflicts at high-injury intersections; effect varies by site (verify locally).
recommended_interventions.trigger: turning conflicts: drivers/passengers are 57% of KSI

recommended_interventions.name: 20 mph default speed limit
recommended_interventions.effect: Part of Hoboken's and London's Vision Zero approach; pedestrian survival probability is far higher in a 20 mph than a 30+ mph impact.
recommended_interventions.trigger: speed is the key driver of crash severity

properties.equity_notes: Serves Ward 1, Ward 4. HIN Tier 1. Equity context is ward-level; pair with DC Equity Emphasis Areas before prioritizing.
properties.confidence_note: 2449 crashes joined within 25 m; 56 KSI (4 killed). Counts from Open Data DC; corridor extent per DDOT HIN.
